name: Tests and WhatsApp channel runbook
description:
## Context
The WhatsApp channel is the first external transport in this repo, so both automated coverage and an operator runbook are needed. Uncertainties to resolve while writing it: the Groups API surface/rollout (the doc page could not be fetched during planning) and the messaging-window rules that apply to DMs vs groups.

## Objective
Test suite + runbook for the WhatsApp bridge.

## Steps
1. `tests/channels/`:
   - `test_store.py`, `test_whatsapp_client.py`, `test_formatting.py` (owned by their tasks — keep the fixtures here);
   - `test_webhook.py`: handshake, HMAC signature valid/invalid, payload normalization, idempotent replay;
   - `test_bridge.py`: inbound → chat message (author mapping, group prefix), outbound → sink (no echo, direction filters, disabled binding);
   - `test_groups.py`: participant sync and join-request approval with a mocked client.
2. Runbook (project doc): creating the Meta app, adding the WhatsApp product, phone number registration, permanent system-user token in `CODX_JUNIOR_WHATSAPP_TOKEN`, app secret in `CODX_JUNIOR_WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`, verify token, subscribing the webhook fields (`messages`, and whatever the group events require), public HTTPS requirement (ngrok for local testing).
3. Document the caveats: group support scope/availability, DM 24-hour customer-service window and template requirement for business-initiated DMs, rate limits, media size limits, and what breaks when the token expires.
4. Add a troubleshooting matrix: signature mismatch, 401 token errors, unbound conversation, group not found, duplicate messages.

## Files
- tests/channels/test_webhook.py (new)
- tests/channels/test_bridge.py (new)
- tests/channels/test_groups.py (new)
- project docs (runbook)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pytest tests/channels` passes locally without network access.
- [ ] Runbook lets a new operator connect a number and a group from scratch.
- [ ] Caveats and the group-support uncertainty are written down with links.
- [ ] Troubleshooting matrix covers the five failure modes above.
